tasks.title: GPS UART load
tasks.statement: Betaflight (the message set was verified on the 4.5-maintenance branch, code = release 4.5.5) has configured a u-blox for **{f} Hz**: NAV-PVT (92 bytes of payload + 8 of overhead) every cycle and NAV-SAT (16 + 12·N bytes) every 5th cycle. NAV-SAT has **N = {n}** satellites, the port is **{b} baud**, 8N1 (10 bits per byte). What is the channel load in percent?
tasks.solution: Bytes per second: f·100 + (f/5)·(16 + 12N). Bits: ×10 (start, 8 data, stop). Load = bit/s ÷ baud × 100. Example: 10 Hz, 28 satellites, 57600 → 17040 bit/s → 29.6 %. At 19200 (the SoftSerial limit) the same gives 88.8 % — no margin.

tasks.title: Distance to home by the Betaflight formula
tasks.statement: Home was recorded on arming. The aircraft is now north of home by **{dlat}** and east by **{dlon}** units of 1e-7° (that is how `gpsSol` stores coordinates), and the latitude of home is **{lat}°**. Find the distance to home in meters by `GPS_distance_cm_bearing()` (2025.12, the formula is the same as in 4.5): d[cm] = √(Δlat² + (Δlon·cos lat)²) · 1.113195.
tasks.solution: 1e-7° of latitude = 1.113195 cm. Longitude shrinks as cos(latitude) (`GPS_scaleLonDown`, computed when home is recorded). Example: Δlat = 3000, Δlon = 4000 at 50°: √(3000² + (4000·0.6428)²) = 3951 → ×1.113195 = 4398 cm ≈ 44.0 m.

tasks.title: Trust in the GPS altitude
tasks.statement: In `flight/position.c` (2025.12, the same in 4.5) the weight of GPS when blending altitude with the baro is gpsTrust = min(1/PDOP, 0.9) (0.3 by default if PDOP is unknown). The module reports **PDOP = {p}**. What is gpsTrust?
tasks.solution: In the code gpsTrust = 100 / pdop, where pdop is stored ×100, that is 1/PDOP. Then MIN(gpsTrust, 0.9): the baro always gets at least 10 %. PDOP 1.35 → 0.74; PDOP ≤ 1.11 → 0.9 (the ceiling); at PDOP 3.3 the weight of 0.30 equals the default.
